audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Yone's E 'Spirit Rewind' — a fabricated name — and describes Spirit Cleave (W) as 'just chip and wave-push', omitting that it shields him.
audit.why: Riot: the E is Soul Unbound (22/19/16/13/10s), spirit leaves the body and repeats a portion of the damage dealt when it snaps back. Spirit Cleave is a flat 14s and 'Grants a shield to Yone', scaling with champions hit — that shield is exactly what eats a Fiora burst window, which is why missingInteractions flags shield-absorbs-burst here.
audit.corrected: Renamed the E to Soul Unbound in mid; early now names Spirit Cleave and its 14s shield; the knockup is attributed to Mortal Steel's second stack; cooldowns added.

edits.before: Yone is even at level 1 but you own the very early scrap — your Q-Vital poke plus the threat of Riposte beats his single-target Q1/Q2 and W cleave before he has the third Q stack. The trap to dodge: his Q3 is the empowered dash that knocks up, so save W for that cast — parrying an immobilizing effect turns the return into a STUN and hands you the trade outright. Don't burn Riposte on his W spirit-cleave; it's just chip and wave-push, not a kill threat. Get to your level 2-3 Q+E and his poke can't keep pace with your Vital sustain.
edits.after: Yone is even at level 1 but you own the very early scrap — your Q-Vital poke plus the threat of Riposte beats his single-target Mortal Steel before he has the second stack. The trap to dodge: that stacked Q is the empowered dash that knocks up, so save W for that cast — parrying an immobilizing effect turns the return into a STUN and hands you the trade. Don't burn Riposte on Spirit Cleave; it is chip and wave-push, but it shields him every 14s, so bait it before you commit. Get to your level 2-3 Q+E and his poke cannot keep pace.

edits.before: This is your window. Every Vital you proc shaves your Q cooldown, so you chain Lunges faster than he can reposition between his W stances. At 6, Grand Challenge marks all four Vitals at once — bait his Q3 dash or his R knockup into Riposte, eat the parry-stun, then circle his four sides for the heal-and-haste zone and the duel is yours. His E (Spirit Rewind) is the one out you must respect: he places a marker, trades, and snaps back to it out of your range — so commit your R only when his E is down or he's already inside your Lunge range with nowhere to rewind to safely.
edits.after: This is your window. Every Vital you proc shaves your Q cooldown, so you chain Lunges faster than he can reposition between cleaves. At 6, Grand Challenge marks all four Vitals at once — bait his stacked Mortal Steel dash or his R into Riposte, eat the parry-stun, then circle his four sides for the heal-and-haste zone and the duel is yours. His E (Soul Unbound) is the one out you must respect: his spirit leaves the body, trades, and snaps back to it out of your range — so commit R only when that E is down, on its 22s at rank 1, or he is already cornered.

edits.before: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Yone, AA once, and E-slow out — repeat until his bar forces the all-in he loses.
edits.after: Mortal Steel's 2nd stack is the empowered knockup dash — parry that cast and your return becomes a stun.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Unbound repeats his damage on the snap-back — be gone by then.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — He snaps back when it ends. Duel him there. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5 — he snaps back when it ends. Duel him there. - Mortal Steel: a flat 4s; the 2nd stack knocks up. - Spirit Cleave: 14s, and it shields him. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

notes: 'Spirit Rewind' was a fabricated ability name in the mid text — the E is Soul Unbound. Riot's R text (Fate Sealed) describes a blink behind the last champion in a line that pulls enemies toward him; the page repeatedly calls it a knockup. A pull is a displacement either way, so the Riposte advice still holds, but calling it a knockup is loose — I left those strings alone rather than assert the CC type from a tooltip.
